children: South Korea’s Samsung E&A has secured a $3.5 billion engineering, procurement and construction (EPC) contract from Saudi Arabia’s SABIC Agri-Nutrients Company for the SAN-7 project in Jubail Industrial City.
Samsung E&A said in a press statement that the 4.7 trillion Korean won ($3.5 billion) contract, signed on Wedesday, will be executed solely by the company, with completion scheduled for 2030.

The facility will use natural gas as feedstock to produce 3,500 metric tonnes per day of ammonia, which will be used to manufacture 7,700 metric tonnes per day of urea fertiliser. The entire urea output is intended for export.
The project will incorporate a post-combustion carbon capture (PCCC) system, enabling carbon dioxide generated during ammonia production to be utilised in urea synthesis, according to Samsung E&A.

The contract adds to Samsung E&A’s recent order intake in the Middle East, which included a $2.4 billion hydrocarbon project in February 2026 and a $790 million water treatment project in June. The company said it is also bidding for several other projects in the Gulf region, including fertiliser and gas facilities.

title: Samsung E&A confirms $3.5bln EPC contract for SABIC Agri-Nutrients project in Saudi Arabia
